picks.title: Ordinary Mind is the Way
picks.summary:
In this Wednesday night Dharma talk, Sensei Koshin Flint Sparks explores a simple and radical teaching: our ordinary experience is itself the awakened way. By ordinary, he means not our passing thoughts but the unmanipulated mind that holds them. Many of us come to practice believing that awakening lies somewhere else, in a later time, a better state, or in exceptional people unlike ourselves.
Source
picks.reason: Explores ordinary mind as the awakened way, a core Zen and Taoist insight.

picks.showTitle: Zen Stories & Buddhist Teachings for Sleep by Midnight Monk
picks.title: Fall Asleep to Buddhist Tales for Peace - A Gentle Journey through Zen Buddhism
picks.summary: Tonight we slow down with the wisdom of Zen Buddhism and the timeless teachings of the Buddha, for anyone whose mind is still busy long after the day has ended. Through gentle Zen stories, Buddhist teachings and calm reflections, we explore how to stop fighting with our thoughts, loosen our grip on what we cannot control, and find the inner peace that has been within reach all along.This 3-hour sleep audio moves softly through some of the most practical ideas in Buddhism: the nature of the mind, letting go, impermanence, beginner's mind, contentment, and surrender. picks.reason: Gentle Zen Buddhist stories and teachings on mind and peace for inner stillness.

picks.title: Being real
picks.summary:
In this Wednesday Night Dharma Talk, Frank Ostaseski traces what he learned sitting at the bedside of thousands of dying people: “to sit next to people and not mess with them. Not try and help them have some experience, or meet someone else’s agenda, including their own. Just sit with them.” That same quality of presence, he suggests, is what it means to ‘be real’ — an alignment with reality…
Source
picks.reason: Teaches presence and being real through sitting with dying people, a contemplative practice.
